## OpenAI

### Simpler API Usage Tiers: Build, Launch, and Grow

Billing just got easier to follow, because OpenAI cut its API usage tiers from five down to three .

The new tiers are Build, Launch, and Grow. Organizations now move between them automatically once their total credit purchases reach the next tier’s minimum.

That means fewer tier rules to track when you plan spend and manage billing. Your organization’s tier also follows your total credit purchases without any manual step.

### Pick the Right GPT-6 Model and Tune Reasoning Effort to Manage Token Spend

If you’re wondering how to keep GPT-6 costs in check, OpenAI published a practical guide for the GPT-6 family .

The guide covers how to select GPT-6 models, how to tune reasoning effort, and how to coordinate tools in production workflows.

Model choice and effort tuning are two of the main levers for controlling token spend. This gives you a reference for shaping workload economics before usage scales up.

### LegalOn Cuts Estimated Daily Codex Costs by 65%

Want proof that smart model choices can save real money? OpenAI shared how LegalOn cut its estimated daily Codex costs by 65% without slowing down development.

According to the summary, the team matched models to tasks and managed budgets strategically.

It’s a useful example for anyone looking at workload efficiency, since it shows that cost reductions and development speed can go together.

### Decisions API Beta Arrives with gpt-6-luna

High-volume decision workloads may be getting cheaper to run, now that OpenAI has released the Decisions API in beta with gpt-6-luna .

OpenAI claims typed answers are delivered 10x faster than with the Responses API.

Shorter processing time may help cost optimization for workloads that run at high volume. It’s worth testing if your team runs lots of decision-style requests.

### Ultrafast Mode Comes to GPT-6.1 Sol in the Responses API

Need quicker output from your API workloads? OpenAI added Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol in the Responses API .

This mode reduces the time between output tokens.

Lower latency can improve throughput and shorten task duration, which helps with workload efficiency.

### GPT-6 Rolls Out Globally in ChatGPT with Intelligent UI

A new flagship model is landing for users everywhere, as OpenAI announced GPT-6 rolling out globally in ChatGPT with Intelligent UI .

The announcement highlights faster responses and more interactive experiences.

Pricing details weren’t included in the announcement. Still, a major model release from a leading provider is worth watching if you’re thinking about workload efficiency and provider strategy.

### GPT-6 and Intelligent UI Now Rolling Out Across ChatGPT Tiers

The GPT-6 news also shows up in the release notes, where OpenAI launched GPT-6 with Intelligent UI in ChatGPT .

It’s rolling out globally across multiple user tiers and brings new model behavior and interactive capabilities.

Since the model behaves differently, it may change usage patterns and efficiency. That makes it worth factoring into your cost planning.

### chat-latest Snapshot Updated for ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise

Heads up for anyone tracking model changes: OpenAI updated the chat-latest snapshot used in ChatGPT for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users.

This model pointer changes over time. If your organization tracks model drift, benchmarking, or cost and performance governance, you’ll want to keep an eye on it.

### Self-Serve HIPAA Compliance Support Now Available for API Organizations

Setting up HIPAA compliance is now a self-serve step, because OpenAI added an in-product flow in API Organization settings .

Eligible admins can accept the standard BAA and enable HIPAA compliance directly from there.

This is a governance update for enterprise API usage, and it lets admins handle the setup on their own.

## Anthropic

### Claude Haiku 5.5 Is the New Default Haiku Model in Claude Code, with 1M Context

Here’s a pricing update worth a close look: Anthropic added Claude Haiku 5.5 as the new default Haiku model in Claude Code .

It comes with 1M context and published pricing of $0.10/$0.50 per Mtok (million tokens). Rates are higher for prompts over 100K tokens.

The published rates and the higher pricing for longer prompts matter for token economics. They also help you decide which workloads should run on this model.

### Claude Code v2.1.288 Brings Better Usage Visibility and Spend Accounting Fixes

Keeping an eye on usage got a bit easier, since Claude Code v2.1.288 added several usage and spend-related improvements .

The release includes a better /usage view for MCP server crediting and improved model-fallback handling.

It also fixed spend-meter accounting in the Claude apps gateway for prompt cache writes and for streamed turns with server-side tools. With those fixes, spend figures should be more accurate.

### Claude Code v2.1.291 and v2.1.290 Add Metadata for Observability and Cost Attribution

If you’re tracing costs in agent workflows, Claude Code v2.1.291 and v2.1.290 have some useful additions .

Anthropic fixed regressions in cloud sessions and added new hook and tool metadata, including serverToolUses , agentId , and ceiling fields. Adjacent releases also include OpenTelemetry span improvements.

These changes help with observability and cost attribution in agent workflows.

### Claude Code v2.1.292 Speeds Up Startup and Improves Background Agent Behavior

Agent-heavy teams might appreciate Claude Code v2.1.292 , which focuses on smoother runs.

It includes faster startup for claude -p and SDK sessions and better handling of overloaded requests. It also has multiple fixes for background agents and scheduled tasks.

Together, these changes can improve operational efficiency and reduce wasted runtime in agent-heavy deployments.

## Google Cloud

### Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 Join Gemini Enterprise AI Developer Tools

Two more models are available in Google’s tooling, as Google added Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 to Gemini Enterprise AI developer tools .

Third-party inference is billed as consumption on Cloud Billing and counts toward the project spend cap. The models are available in the global, US, and EU locations.

That means the usage shows up in your existing billing and is covered by your project’s spend cap.

### Pay-as-You-Go Usage Above Quota Now Covers More Gemini Enterprise Editions

Running out of pooled quota doesn’t have to stop your teams, since Google Cloud added pay-as-you-go usage above quota for Gemini Enterprise Frontline, EDU, and Emerging Market editions .

Once pooled quota limits are reached, organizations can continue usage at pay-as-you-go rates.

That’s handy for cost control and spend management, because overage is billed at pay-as-you-go rates.

### Admins Can Now Turn Antigravity Features On or Off in Gemini Enterprise

You now have more say over who uses what, because Google added admin controls for Antigravity features in Gemini Enterprise .

Admins can enable or disable Boost (generally available) and Teamwork (Preview).

This helps organizations govern access to potentially costly multi-agent workflows and restrict usage where needed.

### Knowledge Catalog Integration Lands in Preview for Gemini Enterprise Data Cloud Connectors

Finding the right data may get quicker, as Google added Knowledge Catalog integration in Preview for Gemini Enterprise Data Cloud connectors .

It gives you read-only tools to search for accessible data and retrieve technical and business context.

This may improve workflow efficiency and reduce duplicated data discovery work.
